rows.en: What you get

rows.en: Your team's own Civicsmith, running in your own Cloudflare account, at your own web address.
rows.note: DEC-338: B323 5: bio-plane/public/newgroup/index.html (the invitation page): list item

rows.en: Full control: your passwords, your credentials, your data. No one else, the publisher of Civicsmith releases included, holds a key to any of it or can see inside it.

rows.en: The Workers Paid plan, $5 a month from Cloudflare. Your team's Civicsmith reads documents and assembles evidence, and the free plan's processing allowance is too small for that work.
rows.note: DEC-338: B323 5: bio-plane/public/newgroup/index.html (the invitation page): list item; the words up to the first comma are bold

rows.en: A payment method on the account. Cloudflare requires one before it turns on the file storage your team's Civicsmith keeps its evidence in. The installer checks for the plan and the storage before it creates anything, and stops, saying which is missing, if either is.
rows.note: DEC-338: B323 5: bio-plane/public/newgroup/index.html (the invitation page): list item; the first sentence is bold

rows.en: The Workers Containers permission, which the setup asks for. It installs the built-in file scanner and safe view: without it, files are kept and shown but not scanned, and a high-risk file opens only in its safe view once one can be made. Everything else installs either way.
rows.note: DEC-338: B323 5: bio-plane/public/newgroup/index.html (the invitation page): list item; the words up to the first comma are bold

rows.en: For the assistant, a Claude plan with cloud sessions, which an organization can turn off. The assistant is optional, and the installer takes no Claude credential of any kind.
rows.note: DEC-338: B323 5: bio-plane/public/newgroup/index.html (the invitation page): list item; the words up to the second comma are bold

rows.en: About twenty minutes, in a browser. No terminal, no code, nothing to download.
rows.note: DEC-338: B323 5: bio-plane/public/newgroup/index.html (the invitation page): list item; the words up to the first comma are bold

rows.en: What happens, and what we can and cannot see
rows.note: DEC-338: B323 5: bio-plane/public/newgroup/index.html (the invitation page): heading

rows.en: The installer asks Cloudflare to show you a permission screen naming exactly what it may do in your account: install the software, set up its storage, and set up the containers for the file scanner and safe view. You approve it on Cloudflare's own page, and you can revoke it any time from your dashboard.
rows.note: DEC-338: B323 5: bio-plane/public/newgroup/index.html (the invitation page): paragraph

rows.en: That permission passes through the installer for the seconds the installation takes, is stored nowhere, and is never seen by a person. After setup, nothing your team does routes through the installer, or its publisher, at all.
rows.note: DEC-338: B323 5: bio-plane/public/newgroup/index.html (the invitation page): paragraph

rows.en: Prefer that nothing pass through the installer even once? The manual path is documented and permanently supported, using only the Cloudflare dashboard. It exists so your team could stand its Civicsmith up even if the publisher of Civicsmith releases disappeared tomorrow. Find it in the project documentation.
rows.note: DEC-338: B323 5: bio-plane/public/newgroup/index.html (the invitation page): small paragraph

rows.en: the source team is named by its slug, and this manifest states {value}
rows.note: DEC-355: B362, reviewed from code (K3930, K4066): "group" for the team written as "team"; American spelling (DEC-221)

rows.en: A member takes every act that commits the team: declaring a standard, determining, assessing a consequence or a success, choosing an option, approving, sending, advancing or stopping a stage, resolving, closing.
rows.note: DEC-355: B362, reviewed from code (K3930, K4066): "group" for the team written as "team"; American spelling (DEC-221)

rows.en: a procedure guide lists the routes the profile or the team knows for one kind of action, in its order and unranked, with the replies to expect and each route's citation; it is legal information, not legal advice, and never how the AI may behave: the AI's rules of conduct come only from the rules Bob approves, no guide can loosen them, and code checks that none does.
rows.note: DEC-355: B362, reviewed from code (K3930, K4066): "group" for the team written as "team"; American spelling (DEC-221)

rows.en: A sentence that asserts a breach as the team's finding needs a live noncompliant determination.
rows.note: DEC-355: B362, reviewed from code (K3930, K4066): "group" for the team written as "team"; American spelling (DEC-221)

rows.en: A version may be written for a particular audience (the violating party, the team's members, an oversight office, the public) or broadly for all.
rows.note: DEC-355: B362, reviewed from code (K3930, K4066): "group" for the team written as "team"; American spelling (DEC-221)

rows.en: Administrators, or members given the grant, have a translation workspace listing every interface word beside the team's language, gaps marked; the assistant drafts the missing ones as labeled drafts, a member who knows the language checks and adopts each, and without the assistant members type them.
rows.note: DEC-355: B362, reviewed from code (K3930, K4066): "group" for the team written as "team"; American spelling (DEC-221)

rows.en: Civicsmith takes no position on what policy should be, and does not rule on policy even when members or teams do.
rows.note: DEC-355: B362, reviewed from code (K3930, K4066): "group" for the team written as "team"; American spelling (DEC-221)

rows.en: Claims about a body rest on findings of the three kinds in §3 or on the team's own dated correspondence; statements about what the team itself is doing need neither.
rows.note: DEC-355: B362, reviewed from code (K3930, K4066): "group" for the team written as "team"; American spelling (DEC-221)

rows.en: Counsel may be briefed at any stage, for a claim or for the team's defense, without a determination
rows.note: DEC-355: B362, reviewed from code (K3930, K4066): "group" for the team written as "team"; American spelling (DEC-221)

rows.en: Every plan for an infraction also offers the violating party the chance to fix and remediate: a notice saying what correcting the act and remedying its harm would look like, with the law's period or a time the team sets.
rows.note: DEC-355: B362, reviewed from code (K3930, K4066): "group" for the team written as "team"; American spelling (DEC-221)

rows.en: No fact and no rule from the model's knowledge; every rule from the plane (system rules from affordances, the team's rules from its reads, jurisdiction rules from the profile, law's text from `standards`); "not held" at its level, with the act that would find it; quotes beside every summary
rows.note: DEC-355: B362, reviewed from code (K3930, K4066): "group" for the team written as "team"; American spelling (DEC-221)

rows.en: no reading guide was passed to this render: a guide is the team's or Civicsmith's, read for the kind of document a run reads by the run's caller, and with none this layer carries nothing to read for.
rows.note: DEC-355: B362, reviewed from code (K3930, K4066): "group" for the team written as "team"; American spelling (DEC-221)

rows.en: Outward acts are classed by what their text does: asking an office to examine something, seeking evidence (a records request, a request for comment), and enforcing the team's own request on its own dated record are never held back.
rows.note: DEC-355: B362, reviewed from code (K3930, K4066): "group" for the team written as "team"; American spelling (DEC-221)

rows.en: Suggested options come from reasoning over the matter, the routes the profile's guides list and the team's own earlier plans, never from a fixed catalog; the plan holds no costs, assignees or hours (members take up work themselves, rule 20).
rows.note: DEC-355: B362, reviewed from code (K3930, K4066): "group" for the team written as "team"; American spelling (DEC-221)

rows.en: The AI may read a document the team holds a few pages at a time, within a reading limit, and never one under a "no AI" limit.
rows.note: DEC-355: B362, reviewed from code (K3930, K4066): "group" for the team written as "team"; American spelling (DEC-221)

rows.en: the fixed terms (the grades, "Undetermined", the queue's kinds, the acts' names) each carry a note on what they mean, so every language says the same thing; renaming words within a language stays out (option A), so cases read the same from team to team.
rows.note: DEC-355: B362, reviewed from code (K3930, K4066): "group" for the team written as "team"; American spelling (DEC-221)

rows.en: the team's own local words are its to translate as ordinary words.
rows.note: DEC-355: B362, reviewed from code (K3930, K4066): "group" for the team written as "team"; American spelling (DEC-221)

rows.en: The team's own writing (notes, questions, findings, notices) can be read in a member's language on request: the assistant drafts the translation, labeled "Machine translation · original in English", with the original one tap away; it never replaces the original.
rows.note: DEC-355: B362, reviewed from code (K3930, K4066): "group" for the team written as "team"; American spelling (DEC-221)

rows.en: the plane's published catalog holds no {id} act, the one act through which a member asks to read the team's own writing in her language, so this layer carries no doctrine for work no draft can do.
rows.note: DEC-355: B362, reviewed from code (K3930, K4066): "group" for the team written as "team"; American spelling (DEC-221)

rows.en: the plane's published catalog holds no {INTERFACE_TRANSLATION_ACT} act, the one act a run drafts the interface words a team's language lacks through, so this layer carries no doctrine for work no run can do.
rows.note: DEC-355: B362, reviewed from code (K3930, K4066): "group" for the team written as "team"; American spelling (DEC-221)

rows.en: The signed statement is the team's, adopted by a member, and the record keeps that it began as a machine draft.
rows.note: DEC-355: B362, reviewed from code (K3930, K4066): "group" for the team written as "team"; American spelling (DEC-221)

rows.en: The system is nonetheless prepared for stonewalling, retaliation, discrediting and legal harassment: every plan is checked for a branch that answers a hostile response; pressure against the team or its supporters is recorded as evidence wherever it arrives, and can open an inquiry of its own; lawful demands are complied with openly.
rows.note: DEC-355: B362, reviewed from code (K3930, K4066): "group" for the team written as "team"; American spelling (DEC-221)

rows.en: this layer is INSTRUCTION. A draft is answered to the member who asked for it, labeled as machine work, and stored nowhere; it never rewrites the member's text, and what it reads is fenced by the modules that serve it. It becomes the team's only by a member's own acts, which refuse a machine. A run ignoring every word here gets past nothing.
rows.note: DEC-355: B362, reviewed from code (K3930, K4066): "group" for the team written as "team"; American spelling (DEC-221)

rows.en: this layer is INSTRUCTION, and this pack reads no account, grant, keep-away setting or word list: which account serves the member, whether the team keeps the assistant away, which member is granted a language and which words a draft is given are read for each call by the modules that serve it. A draft is recorded apart, labeled as machine work, and becomes the team's wording only by a granted member's act. A run ignoring every word here gets past nothing.
rows.note: DEC-355: B362, reviewed from code (K3930, K4066): "group" for the team written as "team"; American spelling (DEC-221)

rows.en: this layer is INSTRUCTION. Every act it names is refused or labeled by the module that performs it: a drafted statement is stored apart and labeled as machine work, and becomes the team's statement only by a member's signing act, which refuses a machine. A run ignoring every word here gets past nothing.
rows.note: DEC-355: B362, reviewed from code (K3930, K4066): "group" for the team written as "team"; American spelling (DEC-221)

rows.en: What the team chose changes only by a member's act.
rows.note: DEC-355: B362, reviewed from code (K3930, K4066): "group" for the team written as "team"; American spelling (DEC-221)

rows.en: What the team sends is checked against its record.
rows.note: DEC-355: B362, reviewed from code (K3930, K4066): "group" for the team written as "team"; American spelling (DEC-221)

rows.en: Wherever a member writes in their own words, the assistant, when reachable, offers "Help me write this": it works only from what the member tells it and what the team holds, never adds a fact (for an observation it only helps word what the member saw), and its words arrive labeled "Draft · the assistant's, asked by" and the asking member's handle, saved only when the member keeps them.
rows.note: DEC-355: B362, reviewed from code (K3930, K4066): "group" for the team written as "team"; American spelling (DEC-221)

rows.en: With the member's suggestions switch off it works only from what the member typed; with it on it may also draw on what the team holds (rule 7).
rows.note: DEC-355: B362, reviewed from code (K3930, K4066): "group" for the team written as "team"; American spelling (DEC-221)

rows.en: Why does my team need its own Cloudflare account?

So that nobody else holds your team's work: the people who make Civicsmith keep none of it and can't open your account. Whoever can sign in to the account controls your team's Civicsmith, so use an account that belongs to your team, and add a second trusted person to it.
What does it cost, who is paid, and how do we stop paying?

About $5 a month for Workers Paid, and R2 storage beyond the 10 GB Cloudflare includes, all paid to Cloudflare only. Nothing is paid to the people who make Civicsmith. To stop paying, cancel Workers Paid in Cloudflare's dashboard. Your team's Civicsmith stops working when the plan ends, so agree on it as a team first.
What can Civicsmith see and do in our account, and how do we remove it?

The installer can create and update your team's Civicsmith's own programs and storage, and nothing else, and it keeps no access afterward. To remove your team's Civicsmith, use the installer's page, or delete its parts in Cloudflare's dashboard, in Workers & Pages and in R2.
Is our card shared with Civicsmith?
No. Your payment method stays with Cloudflare. The installer never sees it, and the permission you give can't reach billing.
What if we already use Cloudflare?

Use that account if it belongs to your team: your team's Civicsmith is added beside what's already there under its own names, nothing else is changed, and the installer checks there is room. If the account is one person's, open a separate one for the team. If it already holds a Civicsmith, the installer says so and asks what you'd like to do.
rows.note: DEC-431: B514 J28 R85 (K4937: a copy already installed)

rows.en: What if we get stuck?

Close the installer at any step and come back: it opens where you left off, and nothing is lost. Cloudflare's own help pages explain each of its steps, and when something is missing, the installer says exactly what.

rewrite.screen.archive.summary: Opened when it was captured: {filed} files filed and held for review beside it, {held} already held, {notfiled} not filed, {folders} folders.
rewrite.screen.archive.alreadyheld: Already held · the same file {name} captured on {date}; this copy is kept as a second sighting of it
rewrite.screen.archive.folder: A folder · its {count} files are listed and filed below it
rewrite.screen.archive.refused.none: Nothing in it is filed. The archive itself stays captured exactly as it arrived, with its grade, and anyone can check why it was refused.
rewrite.screen.calculation.counts: {visited} of {n} visited: {yes} yes, {no} no, {unsure} could not tell
rewrite.screen.calculation.range: {share}% of the {judged} that could be judged were yes · exact {confidence}% range {low}% to {high}%
rewrite.screen.calculation.notsays: It does not recount the {size} ({whose} check did that), says nothing certain about any one {item} no one visited, and nothing about the {outside} {items} not {what}.
rewrite.screen.ceremony.photos.copy: Mark anyone in a photo who is not part of a finding, and any number plate. The public copy shows those areas obscured, labeled “Faces, plates and camera details removed for publication; the team holds the original”, and the original stays inside the team. Every photo a published case carries goes out without its camera details (where and when it was taken, and on which device), labeled “Camera details removed for publication; the team holds the original”. City staff at work are part of what the case is about; obscure one only with a reason.
rewrite.screen.ceremony.signs.count: One confirmation signs all {n}: the edition, its {findings} findings, and the {evidence} pieces of evidence they rest on. Each signature can be checked on its own, so a reader can trust one finding without trusting the rest.
rewrite.screen.docket.sub: The case's public record of corrections, withdrawals and orders.
rewrite.screen.group.court.field: Tell members what a court can reach
rewrite.screen.group-identity.other.field: Describe your kind of team, in a few words
rewrite.screen.group-identity.purpose.field: Why the team exists, in your own words
Also our public page and the network directory
rewrite.screen.held.ineligible: Not included when you vouch for several at once: {reason}
rewrite.screen.held.waiting: {asker}'s question is waiting for {capture}. Your reason is kept on the record and shown to {asker} on the question.
rewrite.screen.help-records.must.1: Answer within {days} days whether it holds records it can release, why or why not, and when they will be ready ({cite}).
rewrite.screen.help-records.must.2: Take longer only by written notice, saying why and when, for reasons the law lists ({reasons}); never more than {extra} extra days ({cite}).
rewrite.screen.help-records.must.3: Help you focus the request: identify the records that fit it, say where they are kept, and suggest ways past practical obstacles ({cite}).
rewrite.screen.help-records.must.4: Release the rest of a record that is partly exempt ({cite}), and refuse only in writing, naming who decided ({cite2}).
rewrite.screen.help-records.must.5: Give electronic records electronically, in a format it keeps them in, when you ask ({cite}).
rewrite.screen.help-records.must.6: Charge only the direct cost of copying ({cite}); for electronic records, of producing the copy, unless it must compile, extract or program data ({cite2}). You may photograph records you inspect, with your own equipment, at no charge ({cite3}).
rewrite.screen.help-records.must.7: Never ask why you want them: access can't be limited because of the purpose of a request ({cite}).
rewrite.screen.help-records.portal.2: Each request's page shows its full text to anyone, with its dates, the department and the city's contact. Write the request so you are content for anyone to read it.
rewrite.screen.help-records.portal.3: Contact details are optional. Without them you get no updates, and you can collect the records only if the department posts them publicly or you contact it yourself.
rewrite.screen.join.language.help: Chosen from your device's setting. You can change it any time.
rewrite.screen.join.handle.help: The record shows your handle on your work. Choose it with care: it can't be changed after you join, and no one else can ever take it. It needn't be your legal name. Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, 2 to 41 of them, starting with a letter or digit. Choosing a handle: a name people know lends your work credibility and lets reporters reach you, but puts it on public cases; a pen name shields you from pressure, while the administrators still know who you are.
rewrite.screen.join.codes.after: When you join, you get ten recovery codes, shown once: save them, they are how you get back in if you forget your password. Then you are signed in and your team's home opens, with a short guided start you can take or leave.
rewrite.screen.money.gap.to: Undetermined: not stated in {source}, the only source holding this figure.
rewrite.screen.people.notmembers: The people and organizations your team's record follows: officials, staff, companies and public bodies. Your own team's members are not listed here; they are under Settings › Members.
rewrite.screen.people.today.seeded: added at setup, from the public offices of your team's place
rewrite.screen.person.expunge.statement: This removes the recorded value for good. It cannot be undone, by you or anyone: the value is gone from this page, from every question that cited it, and from every export. A marker stays where it was: "Removed where the law requires, {date}, by {member}". Published cases are not changed; a court order for those is complied with on the docket.
rewrite.screen.places.wanted.field: A place you want that isn't listed (optional)
rewrite.screen.places.wanted.help: Kept in your team's Civicsmith and never sent anywhere. When an update brings its rules and offices, administrators are told once in their queue and can choose it above.
rewrite.screen.proceeding.login.note: The court's register needs a login, so new filings come only by a member's own capture.
rewrite.screen.projectai.account.suspended: Your sign-in no longer serves {project}. A second member joined, and a sign-in serves a project only while it has one member. Members' acts here now use their own accounts, or the team's key. Add an API key to give the project its own account again; if the project returns to just you, your sign-in serves it again.
rewrite.screen.projectai.notice.head: Before your first question here
rewrite.screen.recovery.held: You hold recovery codes: {remaining} of {total} unused, issued {date}.
rewrite.screen.recovery.shown: Save these now: they are shown only this once. Keep them somewhere only you can reach, apart from your password. Civicsmith keeps only a fingerprint of each, so it can never show them again.
rewrite.screen.reset.keeps: Your handle and everything you did stay as they are, and every other sign-in of yours ends. {name} can't see the password you choose. Your recovery codes still work; if you have lost them too, get ten new ones in Settings › Recovery codes once you are in.
rewrite.screen.reset.dead.what: It was used already, it expired, or an administrator withdrew it. Ask an administrator for a new one, in person or however your team talks. Nothing was changed.
rewrite.screen.review-copy.heading: Share this edition for review
rewrite.screen.review-outside.heading: A review copy from {group}
rewrite.screen.request.describe: Describe the records, not why you want them. The law doesn't let the office limit access because of why you ask ({cite}), and the city's portal shows this text to anyone.
rewrite.screen.request.howsend.1: Open the city's public records portal ({portal}) and choose “{button}”.
rewrite.screen.request.howsend.2: Paste the approved text as the request description, and choose the department: {department}.
rewrite.screen.request.howsend.3: Contact details are optional. Without them the request still goes in, but the city can't send you updates or ask you to clarify, and you can't sign in to collect the records. Give the address your team uses for its requests; staff see what you give.
rewrite.screen.standard.notyet: Not a standard until a member adopts it.
rewrite.screen.ties.says.name.choice: Naming me by my handle: “{handle}, who worked on this case, is {tie}.”
rewrite.screen.ties.says.group.choice: Without naming me: “A member of the team who worked on this case is {tie}.”
rewrite.screen.timeline.order.evidence: More evidence could order them: a passage that gives either one its day (a ledger entry, a meeting's agenda, a letter's date), or a source that says which came first. Until a source orders them, both are kept as they are, never guessed into order; when one does, the timeline names it, and a source that disagrees is shown beside it, in tension.
rewrite.shell.unavailable.nothing.says: This address doesn't lead to anything in your team's Civicsmith. It may have been typed wrong, or the link is old.
rewrite.shell.unavailable.notyours.says: It exists, or it may not: either way it isn't something you can see. A hidden project shows only to its own members; ask its owner if you think you should be in it.
rewrite.shell.unavailable.unreachable.title: Your team's Civicsmith can't be reached
rewrite.shell.unavailable.unreachable.says: Your device is offline, or your team's Civicsmith isn't answering. Nothing you did is lost: what you saved is kept there, and what you were typing is still on this page.
rewrite.screen.wizards.copy.note: A copy becomes your team's own wizard: a draft until approved, like any wizard your team writes. The original stays as it is and is still offered; a required wizard stays required. The copy shows what it is based on, and when Civicsmith's original changes, your wizard editors are told and can bring the change across.
rewrite.screen.setup.lede: Welcome. Civicsmith is installed and waiting for you. First, claim it, so that only you can run it; it takes about two minutes. Then tell it a little about your team. Only the claim is needed today: every other part starts with a safe choice, and you can change any of it later in Settings.
rewrite.screen.setup.otp.help: Already filled in if you came straight from the installer.
rewrite.screen.setup.handle.help: The name you sign in with, shown on your work and on every case you sign. Choose it with care: it can't be changed later.
rewrite.screen.setup.own.help: At least 12 characters. From now on you sign in with your handle and this password.
rewrite.screen.setup.name.help: Shown at the top of every page, on invitations and on everything your team publishes. You can change it any time.
rewrite.screen.setup.name.now: Saved. Your team is now called {name}.
rewrite.screen.setup.domain.help: Civicsmith gives you one small file to put on your website. Once it's there, anyone reading what your team publishes can check that it really comes from you. Whoever looks after your website can do this in a few minutes.
rewrite.screen.setup.places.help: Not listed? Choose “Somewhere else”. Everything still works; you enter deadlines and offices yourself.
rewrite.screen.setup.places.chosen: You chose {place} when you installed. Change it if you need to.
rewrite.screen.setup.place.wanted.help: When an update brings its rules, Civicsmith tells you, and you can switch to it here. What you type stays in your team's Civicsmith and is never sent anywhere.
rewrite.screen.setup.offices.what: Civicsmith can fill in the public offices of {place}, and who holds each one today, from the place's own records. Check the list, then confirm it. You can add others at any time.
rewrite.screen.setup.offices.none: Civicsmith doesn't know the offices of {place} yet, so this list starts empty. Add the offices your team deals with, now or whenever they come up. When an update brings their rules, you'll be told, and the offices you added stay.
rewrite.screen.setup.office.note: Anything your team should know about it (optional)
rewrite.screen.setup.assistant.what: Civicsmith can include an AI assistant, built on Anthropic's Claude. Members ask it, in everyday words, to find, read and check things in your team's material. It works only from what your team holds, gives legal information but never legal advice, and never decides, signs or sends anything. Everything in Civicsmith also works without it.
rewrite.screen.setup.keepaway: No, keep our material away from AI
rewrite.screen.setup.keepaway.help: Required. Every member will see it.
rewrite.screen.setup.assistant.own: A member who wants the assistant connects their own Claude subscription or API key. It serves only them, at their own cost, and costs your team nothing.
rewrite.screen.setup.assistant.paid: One Anthropic API key, paid for by your team, serves every member who has no account of their own. A member's own account still comes first.
rewrite.screen.setup.key.help: Made in Anthropic's Console, under an account your team pays for. Civicsmith locks it away and never shows it again.
rewrite.screen.setup.limit: The most each member may use per day
rewrite.screen.setup.limit.help: Applies only to your team's key, never to a member's own account. More limits are in Settings › Members.
rewrite.screen.setup.people.what: Facts about a person that come from public documents are as visible as those documents are. Your team's own notes about a person stay inside the project where they were written.
rewrite.screen.setup.court.what: Civicsmith keeps your team's unpublished work private, from the public and from the people you look into. But a court order your team can't defeat can still require anything not public to be shown, such as members' notes, sources and hidden projects. Much work never draws such an order, and journalists, lawyers and auditors may have protections others lack.
rewrite.screen.setup.court.legend: Should members be told about this?
rewrite.screen.setup.court.tell: Yes, when they join, and the first time they save something not public
rewrite.screen.setup.court.dont: No, just keep the explanation one tap away
rewrite.screen.setup.admins.what: Right now you're the only administrator. If you're away or lose access, no one else can run your team's Civicsmith. Invite someone you trust as a second administrator, now or later.
rewrite.screen.setup.security.scanner: Civicsmith's own file scanner checks every file your team brings in, and risky ones open in a safe view. You don't need to do anything.
rewrite.screen.setup.security.what: If your organization already uses its own file scanner, a tool that makes safe copies of files, or a log service, you can connect it here or later in Settings › Security.
rewrite.screen.setup.finished.what: Anything you left is waiting in Settings. Next, invite your first members.
rewrite.act.queuemute.does: Stops this kind of item, or a project's items, reaching your queue, or lets muted ones reach it again. What you muted is listed under Muted at the foot of your queue.
rewrite.act.promote.does: Turns what you are looking at into something the team will work on: a hint, chain or suggestion into a question, or a problem into a project. Where it came from is kept with it.
rewrite.project.visibility.start.later: Choose one: neither is chosen for you. You can change it later, with a reason.
rewrite.screen.updates.admins: Only your team's administrators install updates. Yours: {admins}. If something needs updating, ask one of them.
rewrite.screen.security.admins: Security is set by your team's administrators. Yours: {admins}. Ask one of them about anything here.
rewrite.question.empty.heading: Next: bring in a source
rewrite.question.empty.note: A question is answered from documents: your government's own records, a report, what a member saw. Start with one; you can add more at any time.
rewrite.question.empty.capture.line: Its web address, a file, or what you saw yourself. Civicsmith keeps the copy for you to confirm, then you mark the part that answers.
rewrite.question.empty.find.line: Search the team's documents, open one, and mark the part that answers.
rewrite.question.empty.ask.line: It reads what the team holds and suggests the parts that answer, and an answer. Nothing counts until a member accepts it.
rewrite.stake.none: No stake of its own beyond the team's
rewrite.screen.review-copy.until.nozone: Your team's time zone isn't set, and a review link's end date is counted in it. Set it under Settings, Your team, then share.
rewrite.refusal.ACCOUNT_MEMBER_NOT_ACTIVE: Your membership isn't active in your team's Civicsmith just now, so this can't go ahead. Nothing was sent. An administrator can tell you why.
rewrite.refusal.NO_SAFE_VIEW: Your team's Civicsmith makes safe views of documents, presentations, spreadsheets and plain text, and this file is none of them, so it has no safe view.
rewrite.refusal.MACHINE_CANNOT_MARK: Only a member, acting for themselves, marks this: a watch, a second look, or a result from a paid or account-gated service. No assistant, scheduled task or unattended process can. Nothing was written.
rewrite.screen.proceeding.kind.help: What kind of proceeding this is. It decides which deadlines and steps Civicsmith suggests; you can change it later.
rewrite.screen.find-in.question: For which question
rewrite.screen.find-in.term.help: Only passages with this name or term are shown, when you fill it in.
rewrite.screen.held.ineligible.alone: Open it to vouch for it by itself. Vouching is your signature that this copy is what its source gave; it then enters the record.
rewrite.screen.inbox.ladder.basis: Unknown: nothing is known of who handed it in. Same knocker: it came with the same secret phrase as earlier material, which says nothing about who they are. Partly known: the team knows something about them, such as an occupation. Known to the team: members know who they are. Public: they are publicly named. This inbox shows only what a secret phrase can tell; anything more is kept with the source.
rewrite.screen.doorbell.received: Received on {at}. A member of the team will read it. Keep the reference and the date: they are all you have to ask about it, because this page does not know who you are.
rewrite.screen.capture.address.existed: Already in the record as {title}: your team holds exactly this document. Nothing new was saved.
rewrite.screen.document.cite.question: Cite in which question
rewrite.screen.finder.widen: Documents holding at least one of the words: {n}.
rewrite.screen.open-file.safe.ready: The safe view is open below: each page as a picture, so nothing in it can run.
rewrite.screen.standard.text.help: Pick the document that states the requirement, as captured. The passage is the whole document until you select its words.
rewrite.screen.review-copy.nodraft: There is no draft to share yet. Make a draft of the case first, then share it.
rewrite.screen.start-send.noclock: No legal deadline for this kind of action (your team's profile names none)
rewrite.shell.card.open: Press or tap to open it.
rewrite.screen.home.move.anyone: any member can take the next step
rewrite.screen.matter.proposed: Proposed next: {stage}. Civicsmith proposes; a member decides.
rewrite.screen.matter.advance: Move on to the next stage: {stage}
rewrite.screen.money.f.contract: The contract, for committed against paid
rewrite.screen.held.more: {count} shown here. More are on the next page.
